deep.reconstruction:
Context (cote 154, 1983-84): X is a topological projective plane and X_1 ⊂ X is a system (arrangement) of pseudo-lines with singular set X_0 = S(X_1), the vertices. Grothendieck builds a 2-dimensional cellular space 𝔛 that parametrises a pseudo-line D in general position with respect to X_1. It comes with a map 𝔛 → X and with a parallel transport of pseudo-line systems (PsDS) along paths in 𝔛. D̃ is a double cover / circle attached to D (the boundary of Pol(D)). A 'demi-cercle' is an arc of D̃ bounded by antipodal points s, s'. Along such an arc one meets 'transition arcs', where the combinatorial position of D relative to X_1 changes, and 'arcs of generalisation / specialisation'.

Property (PS), the special feature of genuine pseudo-line systems: every half-circle arc a of D̃ contains an ordinary transition arc, except in two cases.

(1) The endpoints s, s' of a are endpoints of generalisation arcs α, α'. The point t of X determined by {s, s'} is a vertex of X_1. There is a component D_i of X_1 through t and an orientation ω of X at t such that D is a small perturbation of D_i near t. Then α·(å∩a)·(å'∩a) is the 'rive de balayage' (sweep shore) attached to the triple (D_i, t, ω). In the margin: case v ∈ X_0, where 'a contains a transition arc with no obstruction'. A diagonal NB lists subcases a)–d) (s = s', s ≠ s', distinct, specialisation …) for (D̃_i, β, ω), with arcs T_1, T_2.

(2) The endpoints carry specialisation constraints α_s ∌ α_{s'}. There is an edge β of X_1 lying on a component D_i, and an orientation of β, such that D is deduced from D_i by sweeping. In the margin: case v ∉ X_0, where 'a contains two specialisation arcs'. This case is left unfinished.

Right column, the payoff: (PS) is what made him believe that 𝔛 has only two kinds of vertices. These are the ordinary vertices of order 4, and the 'exceptional' vertices indexed by triples (D_i, β, ω): D_i a component of X_1, β a cell (facet) of D_i, ω an orientation of X along β. Without (PS) one has no control over the types of vertices of 𝔛. In that case it is unclear to what extent the parallel transport on PsDS comes from a local system on 𝔛.

The next page continues with this transport. It relates transport on X and on 𝔛 by τ_X = σ^ν τ_𝔛, where σ is the antipodal map and ν counts crossings of 'superposingular' lines.

In modern terms, this is a local-structure lemma for a cell complex of single-pseudoline extensions of an arrangement. Its aim is to classify the vertex links of that complex, so as to decide whether the monodromy of the arrangement-valued transport is locally constant.
errors: The text explicitly corrects an earlier overstatement (previous page: 'j'ai été un peu vif'): the vertex classification is not as clean as first claimed, and here it is phrased as something he had been led to believe rather than proved.
Case 2) of (PS) is incomplete; the sentence breaks off ('D_i déduits —'). The list of exceptions is therefore not established on this page.
The diagonal NB with subcases a)–d) is partly struck out and visibly provisional. No proof of (PS) is given, and the right column concedes that without it the local-system question is open.

ideas.what: A cellular parameter space 𝔛 of pseudo-lines D in general position relative to a fixed pseudo-line arrangement X_1, with a map 𝔛 → X and combinatorial 'transitions' when D crosses vertices of X_1.
ideas.modern_name: Extension space of a rank-3 oriented matroid / space of one-element pseudo-line extensions of an arrangement
ideas.usually_credited_to: Las Vergnas (single-element extensions, 1978); Sturmfels–Ziegler, 'Extension spaces of oriented matroids' (1993); Mnëv–Ziegler
ideas.where_published: Pseudo-line systems are possibly alluded to in Esquisse d'un programme (1984), section on 'géométrie modérée'/topological geometry; no detailed published account known to me

ideas.what: Lemma (PS): every antipodal half-circle arc on D̃ contains an ordinary transition, except in sweep situations where D is a small perturbation of a component D_i near a vertex t or along an edge β.
ideas.modern_name: Local analysis of mutations / triangle flips (Reidemeister-III-type moves) for pseudo-line extensions; the 'sweep' recalls topological sweeping
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ringel (1956, flip connectivity); Edelsbrunner–Guibas (topological sweep, 1986); Goodman–Pollack (allowable sequences)

ideas.what: Classification of the vertices of 𝔛 into ordinary order-4 vertices and exceptional vertices indexed by (D_i, β, ω): component, cell and orientation.
ideas.modern_name: Vertex/link structure of the cell complex of an extension space (cf. zonotopal-tiling and fiber-zonotope pictures)
ideas.usually_credited_to: unclear; partly implicit in Sturmfels–Ziegler and in work on the Baues problem

ideas.what: Whether the parallel transport of pseudo-line systems along paths in 𝔛 comes from a local system on 𝔛, with an antipodal correction factor σ^ν (next page).
ideas.modern_name: Monodromy / local-coefficient system on the extension space; a twisted transport involving the antipodal map

missed.claim: Grothendieck tries to show that the space 𝔛 of pseudo-line extensions of an arrangement has only two vertex types, using (PS). He then wants to conclude that transport of pseudo-line systems is a local system on 𝔛. He leaves both open.
missed.quote: il s'ensuit qu'il n'est pas clair dans quelle mesure le transport [parallèle] sur les PsDS [provient d']un syst. local sur 𝔛
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Extension spaces of oriented matroids are studied mainly through their homotopy type (Sturmfels–Ziegler) and through the extension-space conjecture. A local-system / parallel-transport viewpoint on them, including the antipodal twist τ_X = σ^ν τ_𝔛, is not a standard tool. It could give monodromy invariants for rank-3 extension spaces.

missed.claim: The page implicitly links the topological-geometric construction of a cell complex 𝔛 → RP² with the combinatorics of oriented-matroid extensions and sweeps. That ties Grothendieck's 'géométrie modérée' programme to the later oriented-matroid literature, which never cites it.
missed.quote: les sommets correspondant aux exceptions (D̃_i, β, ω) … une orientation de X en β
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mainly historical: it documents an independent, topology-first approach to pseudo-line extension spaces by Grothendieck, contemporaneous with or prior to Sturmfels–Ziegler.

deep.surprise_reason: This is an intermediate technical lemma in a little-known programme. The underlying objects (extension spaces of pseudo-line arrangements, flips, sweeps) were later developed independently. The local-system/monodromy angle is somewhat distinctive, but here it is only posed as an open doubt, not developed.
